questionText: Choose the sentence that is correctly formed: 'The committee _____ their decision yesterday.'
options: A) announced
B) announce
C) announcing
D) announces
explanation: Announced is correct for past tense - A-N-N-O-U-N-C-E-D. The committee made an announcement yesterday.

questionText: Complete the sentence: 'Despite the rain, she _____ determined to finish the race.'
options: A) remained
B) remain
C) remaining
D) remains
explanation: Remained is the correct past tense form - R-E-M-A-I-N-E-D. The sentence describes a past action.

questionText: Which sentence uses the subjunctive mood correctly?
options: A) If I were you, I would reconsider.
B) If I was you, I would reconsider.
C) If I am you, I would reconsider.
D) If I be you, I would reconsider.
explanation: If I were you uses the subjunctive mood correctly - W-E-R-E. The subjunctive expresses hypothetical situations.

questionText: Choose the correctly formed sentence with a relative clause:
options: A) The book that I borrowed is fascinating.
B) The book which I borrowed it is fascinating.
C) The book that I borrowed it is fascinating.
D) The book who I borrowed is fascinating.
explanation: That I borrowed is the correct relative clause. Do not add a pronoun after the relative pronoun.

questionText: Complete the sentence: 'Neither the students nor the teacher _____ aware of the problem.'
options: A) was
B) were
C) are
D) been
explanation: Was agrees with the nearest subject teacher - W-A-S. In neither...nor constructions, the verb agrees with the closer subject.

questionText: Which sentence demonstrates correct parallel structure?
options: A) She likes swimming, hiking, and cycling.
B) She likes swimming, to hike, and cycling.
C) She likes to swim, hiking, and cycle.
D) She likes swim, hiking, and to cycle.
explanation: Swimming, hiking, and cycling are all gerunds - parallel structure requires the same grammatical form.

questionText: Complete: 'By the time we arrived, they _____ the entire meal.'
options: A) had finished
B) have finished
C) finished
D) were finishing
explanation: Had finished is the past perfect - H-A-D F-I-N-I-S-H-E-D. It shows an action completed before another past action.

questionText: Which sentence uses a dangling modifier correctly?
options: A) Walking to school, I saw a rainbow.
B) Walking to school, a rainbow was seen.
C) Walking to school, the rainbow appeared.
D) A rainbow appeared, walking to school.
explanation: Walking to school, I saw a rainbow - the modifier correctly refers to I, the subject of the main clause.

questionText: Complete: 'The scientist, along with her colleagues, _____ the results.'
options: A) published
B) published
C) published
D) published
explanation: Published is the correct past tense - P-U-B-L-I-S-H-E-D. Along with her colleagues is a parenthetical phrase that does not change the subject.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses the passive voice?
options: A) The bridge was built in 1920.
B) The bridge built in 1920.
C) The bridge has build in 1920.
D) The bridge is building in 1920.
explanation: Was built is the correct passive voice form - B-U-I-L-T. It uses was + past participle.

questionText: Complete: 'Scarcely had she arrived _____ the phone rang.'
options: A) when
B) than
C) then
D) before
explanation: Scarcely...when is the correct correlative conjunction pair. Scarcely pairs with when, not than.

questionText: Which option correctly completes: 'The data _____ inconclusive'?
options: A) are
B) is
C) were
D) was
explanation: Data is a plural noun - A-R-E. In formal writing, data takes a plural verb. The singular form is datum.

questionText: Identify the correctly formed sentence:
options: A) Whoever finishes first will receive a prize.
B) Whomever finishes first will receive a prize.
C) Whoever finishes first, they will receive a prize.
D) Who finishes first will receive a prize.
explanation: Whoever is correct as the subject of finishes - W-H-O-E-V-E-R. Use whoever when it is the subject of its clause.

questionText: Complete: 'I wish I _____ more time to study for the exam.'
options: A) had
B) have
C) having
D) had had
explanation: Had is the subjunctive form for present wishes - H-A-D. I wish I had expresses a current unreal situation.

questionText: Which sentence uses reported speech correctly?
options: A) She said she was going to the market.
B) She said she is going to the market.
C) She said she will go to the market.
D) She said she goes to the market.
explanation: Was going is the correct backshifted form - W-A-S G-O-I-N-G. In reported speech, the tense shifts back by one.

questionText: Complete: 'The more he practiced, _____ he became.'
options: A) the better
B) better
C) more better
D) the more better
explanation: The more...the better is the correct comparative structure. Both parts use the definite article the.

questionText: Identify the sentence with the correct use of a semicolon:
options: A) He studied hard; consequently, he passed the exam.
B) He studied hard; and he passed the exam.
C) He studied hard; because he wanted to pass.
D) He; studied hard and passed the exam.
explanation: Semicolons correctly join two independent clauses, especially before conjunctive adverbs like consequently.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses an infinitive as a subject?
options: A) To err is human.
B) To err it is human.
C) Erring is human being.
D) To erring is human.
explanation: To err is human correctly uses an infinitive as subject - T-O E-R-R. The infinitive phrase acts as the subject of the sentence.

questionText: Complete: 'No sooner had we left _____ it started raining.'
options: A) than
B) when
C) then
D) after
explanation: No sooner...than is the correct pair - T-H-A-N. No sooner always pairs with than, not when.

questionText: Which sentence uses a gerund phrase correctly?
options: A) Running every morning keeps her healthy.
B) Run every morning keeps her healthy.
C) To running every morning keeps her healthy.
D) Runs every morning keep her healthy.
explanation: Running every morning is a gerund phrase acting as subject - R-U-N-N-I-N-G. Gerunds end in -ing and function as nouns.

questionText: Complete: 'He is the most talented student _____ I have ever taught.'
options: A) that
B) who
C) which
D) whom
explanation: That is used after superlatives in relative clauses - T-H-A-T. Most talented triggers the use of that rather than who.

questionText: Choose the sentence that avoids a split infinitive (formal context):
options: A) She decided to carefully examine the evidence.
B) She decided to carefully to examine the evidence.
C) She carefully decided to examine the evidence.
D) She decided carefully to examine evidence.
explanation: To carefully examine places the adverb inside the infinitive. Formal style sometimes avoids this, but it is widely accepted in modern usage.

questionText: Identify the correctly punctuated sentence:
options: A) Although she studied hard, she did not pass.
B) Although she studied hard she did not pass.
C) Although, she studied hard she did not pass.
D) Although she studied hard: she did not pass.
explanation: A comma follows an introductory subordinate clause - C-O-M-M-A. Although she studied hard is the introductory clause.

questionText: Complete: 'Each of the students _____ expected to submit their project.'
options: A) is
B) are
C) were
D) have
explanation: Is is correct because each is a singular indefinite pronoun - E-A-C-H. Each always takes a singular verb.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses an appositive phrase?
options: A) My sister, a brilliant doctor, works in Chennai.
B) My sister a brilliant doctor works in Chennai.
C) My sister, a brilliant doctor works in Chennai.
D) My sister a brilliant doctor, works in Chennai.
explanation: Appositive phrases are set off by commas on both sides - A-P-P-O-S-I-T-I-V-E. A brilliant doctor identifies my sister.

questionText: Complete: 'It is essential that every participant _____ the rules.'
options: A) follow
B) follows
C) followed
D) following
explanation: Follow is the mandative subjunctive - F-O-L-L-O-W. After essential that, use the base form of the verb without s.

questionText: Which sentence is correctly formed using a conditional type 3?
options: A) If she had studied, she would have passed.
B) If she studied, she would have passed.
C) If she had studied, she would pass.
D) If she has studied, she would have passed.
explanation: If + past perfect, would + have + past participle is the correct Type 3 conditional structure.

questionText: Choose the sentence that correctly positions the adverb:
options: A) He barely spoke during the meeting.
B) He spoke barely during the meeting.
C) Barely he spoke during the meeting.
D) He spoke during barely the meeting.
explanation: Barely correctly precedes the verb it modifies - B-A-R-E-L-Y. Adverbs of frequency and degree usually precede the main verb.

questionText: Complete: 'She would rather _____ at home than go to the party.'
options: A) stay
B) staying
C) stayed
D) to stay
explanation: Would rather is followed by the base form of the verb - S-T-A-Y. Would rather stay uses the bare infinitive.

questionText: Identify the sentence with correct subject-verb agreement:
options: A) A number of students were absent.
B) A number of students was absent.
C) The number of students were absent.
D) The number of students have been absent.
explanation: A number of takes a plural verb were - N-U-M-B-E-R. But the number of takes a singular verb.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses an absolute phrase?
options: A) The work finished, she left the office.
B) The work finishing, she left the office.
C) The work was finished, she left the office.
D) Having finish work, she left the office.
explanation: The work finished is a correct absolute phrase - A-B-S-O-L-U-T-E. It has its own subject and a participial form.

questionText: Complete: 'The old man, _____ son is a doctor, lives next door.'
options: A) whose
B) who
C) whom
D) which
explanation: Whose shows possession - W-H-O-S-E. Whose son indicates that the son belongs to the old man.

questionText: Which sentence demonstrates correct use of ellipsis in conversation?
options: A) John can play the piano, and Mary can too.
B) John can play the piano, and Mary can also play the piano too.
C) John can play the piano, and so does Mary.
D) John can play the piano, and Mary can play also.
explanation: And Mary can too uses ellipsis by omitting the repeated play the piano - E-L-L-I-P-S-I-S.

questionText: Complete: 'The children _____ in the park when it started to rain.'
options: A) were playing
B) played
C) have played
D) play
explanation: Were playing is the past continuous - P-L-A-Y-I-N-G. It describes an ongoing action interrupted by another event.

questionText: Which sentence uses an inverted structure correctly for emphasis?
options: A) Never have I seen such courage.
B) Never I have seen such courage.
C) Never I saw such courage.
D) Never had I see such courage.
explanation: Never have I seen uses correct inversion - N-E-V-E-R. After negative adverbs, invert the auxiliary and subject.

questionText: Complete: 'She has been living here _____ ten years.'
options: A) for
B) since
C) from
D) during
explanation: For is used with a duration of time - F-O-R. Since is used with a specific point in time.

questionText: Identify the sentence that avoids a comma splice:
options: A) She was tired; however, she continued working.
B) She was tired, however she continued working.
C) She was tired, however, she continued working.
D) She was tired however she continued working.
explanation: A semicolon before however correctly joins two independent clauses and avoids a comma splice.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses the future perfect tense?
options: A) By tomorrow, she will have completed the report.
B) By tomorrow, she will complete the report.
C) By tomorrow, she completes the report.
D) By tomorrow, she is completing the report.
explanation: Will have completed is the future perfect - F-U-T-U-R-E P-E-R-F-E-C-T. It shows an action to be completed before a future time.

questionText: Complete: 'It was not until midnight _____ the last guest left.'
options: A) that
B) when
C) which
D) then
explanation: It was not until...that is the correct cleft sentence structure - C-L-E-F-T. This construction adds emphasis.

questionText: Which sentence is formed correctly with a correlative conjunction?
options: A) Both the teacher and the student were present.
B) Both the teacher as well as the student were present.
C) Both the teacher and the student was present.
D) Both the teacher or the student were present.
explanation: Both...and is the correct correlative conjunction pair - C-O-R-R-E-L-A-T-I-V-E. Both...and always takes a plural verb.

questionText: Complete: 'He speaks English as fluently _____ a native speaker.'
options: A) as
B) like
C) than
D) that
explanation: As...as is used for comparisons of equality - A-S. As fluently as correctly compares two equal qualities.

questionText: Identify the correctly formed question:
options: A) Seldom does he miss a class.
B) Seldom he misses a class.
C) Seldom does he misses a class.
D) Seldom he does miss a class.
explanation: Seldom does he miss uses correct inversion with a negative adverb - S-E-L-D-O-M. The auxiliary does precedes the subject.

questionText: Complete: 'I would have helped you if you _____ asked.'
options: A) had
B) have
C) would have
D) would
explanation: Had asked is the past perfect in the if-clause of a Type 3 conditional - H-A-D. This expresses an unreal past condition.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses a noun clause as object?
options: A) I believe that honesty is important.
B) I believe honesty is important that.
C) I believe what is important honesty.
D) I believe that is important honesty.
explanation: That honesty is important is a noun clause as the object of believe - N-O-U-N C-L-A-U-S-E.

questionText: Complete: 'The harder you work, _____ your chances of success.'
options: A) the greater
B) greater
C) the more great
D) greatly
explanation: The harder...the greater is the double comparative structure - C-O-M-P-A-R-A-T-I-V-E. Both parts take the definite article the.

questionText: Which sentence uses an adverbial clause of concession correctly?
options: A) Though he is poor, he is honest.
B) Though he is poor but he is honest.
C) Although he is poor but he is honest.
D) Despite he is poor, he is honest.
explanation: Though he is poor, he is honest uses the concession clause correctly - T-H-O-U-G-H. Never pair though or although with but.

questionText: Identify the sentence with correct use of articles:
options: A) She is an honest officer in the army.
B) She is a honest officer in the army.
C) She is an honest officer in an army.
D) She is a honest officer in an army.
explanation: An is used before honest because H is silent, so it sounds like a vowel - A-N. The army refers to a specific institution.

questionText: Complete: 'I am used to _____ early every morning.'
options: A) waking
B) wake
C) woke
D) waken
explanation: Waking is the gerund form after be used to - W-A-K-I-N-G. Be used to is always followed by a gerund, not an infinitive.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses the present perfect continuous tense?
options: A) She has been studying for three hours.
B) She is studying for three hours.
C) She has studied for three hours now.
D) She studied for three hours continuously.
explanation: Has been studying is the present perfect continuous - C-O-N-T-I-N-U-O-U-S. It shows an ongoing action from the past to now.

questionText: Complete: 'Provided that you _____ on time, you will be admitted.'
options: A) arrive
B) arrived
C) will arrive
D) arriving
explanation: Arrive is the simple present in a conditional clause - A-R-R-I-V-E. After provided that, use simple present for a real condition.
